text: I think a square is not really a rectangle because a rectangle has to be longer than it is wide.
A square can be both a square and a rectangle if the definition is about properties instead of how the picture looks.
The tilted one feels like a diamond, not a square, because squares sit flat on the page.
The drawing changes but the properties do not, so I wonder whether the image or the definition should decide the name.
If the perimeter is bigger then the area should also be bigger, since it goes farther around.
Area is not the shape itself. I am trying to separate the boundary from the region we are measuring.
